title: Behind the Magic
intro: [excited] Welcome to the most HISTORIC episode we have ever done! Tonight it's all about Walt Disney and the Imagineers who built the magic. [chuckles] It all started with a mouse... and tonight it might end with your score.

categories.title: The Mouse That Started It All
categories.intro: Our film category is all about the early cartoons, from Mickey's big debut to Walt's very first Oscar. [whispers] Old school.

clues.clue: Mickey Mouse's famous 1928 sound cartoon shows him whistling as he steers a riverboat.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Steamboat Willie! [excited] November 18, 1928 is considered Mickey's birthday. Fun fact, Plane Crazy was actually made first, but it had no sound.

clues.clue: For nearly two decades, Walt Disney himself provided the voice of this character.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mickey Mouse! [chuckles] Walt voiced him from 1928 until 1947. Donald, meanwhile, was Clarence Nash. Nobody else could make THAT noise.

clues.clue: Before Mickey, Walt created this lucky character, but lost the rights to him in 1928.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Oswald the Lucky Rabbit! [sighs] Not so lucky for Walt. But in 2006 Disney finally got him back in a trade that involved a sportscaster. Seriously.

clues.clue: Legend says Walt first wanted to name his new mouse this, until his wife Lillian suggested Mickey.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mortimer! [laughs] Lillian thought it sounded too pompous. Mortimer Mouse did show up later, though, as Mickey's rival for Minnie.

clues.clue: Walt's first Academy Award came for this 1932 Silly Symphony, the first cartoon released in full three-strip Technicolor.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Flowers and Trees! [gasps] It was originally started in black and white, then Walt had it redone in color. Talk about plussing.

categories.title: Walt's Story
categories.intro: Let's talk about the man himself. Walt's life, from the Midwest to Hollywood. [dramatic pause] How well do you know Uncle Walt?

clues.clue: Walt's older brother, who co-founded the company with him and handled all the money.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Roy O. Disney! [chuckles] Walt dreamed it, Roy figured out how to pay for it. Roy also delayed retirement to finish building Walt Disney World.

clues.clue: Walt Disney was born in 1901 in this big Midwestern city.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Chicago! [excited] December 5, 1901. Then the family moved to a farm in Marceline, Missouri, the town that inspired Main Street U.S.A.

clues.clue: Before moving to Hollywood, Walt ran this Kansas City animation studio, which went bankrupt in 1923.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Laugh-O-Gram Studio! [sighs] Walt was so broke he reportedly lived in the office. Then he bought a train ticket west with what little he had left.

clues.clue: Walt's backyard miniature railroad at his Holmby Hills home was called this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Carolwood Pacific Railroad! [laughs] Named after his street, Carolwood Drive. Its engine was called the Lilly Belle, after Lillian.

clues.clue: When Walt and Roy opened their first Hollywood studio in 1923, it was called this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio! [mischievously] October 16, 1923, the official birthday of the company. Roy, of course, signed the checks.

categories.title: Before and After
categories.intro: It's Before and After! I'll describe two Disney things that share a word. You combine them into one phrase. [laughs] It's harder than it sounds.

clues.clue: Walt's Florida resort meets EPCOT's lagoon ring of eleven nations.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Walt Disney World Showcase! [chuckles] Get it? World, World. Stack 'em up. You're a natural.

clues.clue: A skipper-led boat ride full of terrible puns meets the company's fleet of ocean ships.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Jungle Cruise Line! [laughs] Imagine a whole cruise of skipper jokes. The backside of water, for seven nights.

clues.clue: Mickey's 1928 sound debut meets the giant who steals the magic harp in a 1947 beanstalk tale.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Steamboat Willie the Giant! [gasps] Willie the Giant is from Mickey and the Beanstalk in Fun and Fancy Free. Fee fi fo fum, you got it.

clues.clue: Walt's 1955 TV show for kids with mouse ears meets Disneyland's secret, members-only dining spot in New Orleans Square.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mickey Mouse Club 33! [whispers] Club 33 is the exclusive club Walt planned for VIPs. The waitlist is legendary. M-I-C, see you real soon.

clues.clue: Walt's rotating theater show from the 1964 World's Fair meets the giant scale model of his planned city of tomorrow, the original EPCOT.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Carousel of Progress City! [excited] Progress City was Walt's dream community. The Carousel still spins at Magic Kingdom, with a great big beautiful tomorrow.

categories.title: Opening Day 1955
categories.intro: It's July 17, 1955. Disneyland opens its gates. [dramatic pause] What could possibly go wrong? Spoiler... a lot.

clues.clue: Disneyland opened in 1955 in this Southern California city.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Anaheim! [chuckles] Back then it was orange groves as far as the eye could see. Now it's churros as far as the eye can see.

clues.clue: The castle at the heart of Disneyland is named after this princess.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Sleeping Beauty! [gasps] The castle opened four years BEFORE the movie came out. Talk about marketing.

clues.clue: Along with Main Street, Adventureland, Frontierland, and Fantasyland, this was one of Disneyland's original lands.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Tomorrowland! [laughs] It was so rushed on opening day that Walt covered the empty spots with balloons and banners. The future was... under construction.

clues.clue: Walt had a private apartment above this building on Main Street, U.S.A., and a lamp in the window is still kept lit.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Fire Station! [whispers] When the lamp is on, it means Walt is in the park. And they never turn it off.

clues.clue: Because of melting asphalt, broken drinking fountains, and huge crowds, Disney staff gave opening day this nickname.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Black Sunday! [sighs] Dateline Disneyland was the live TV broadcast that day. Women's high heels were literally sinking into the fresh asphalt.

categories.title: Imagineering 101
categories.intro: The fans asked for nerdy, so we're going behind the berm. [mischievously] Imagineering jargon, tricks, and secrets.

clues.clue: Disney's theme park designers are called this, a mix of the words imagination and engineering.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Imagineers! [excited] Walt Disney Imagineering started back in 1952 as WED Enterprises. W, E, D, for Walter Elias Disney.

clues.clue: Imagineers invented these lifelike robotic figures, which first appeared in 1963 in the Enchanted Tiki Room.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Audio-Animatronics! [laughs] In the tiki tiki tiki tiki tiki room. Dozens of singing birds, flowers, and tiki gods. ALL robots.

clues.clue: Imagineers make Main Street buildings look taller by building each upper floor smaller than the one below, a trick called this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is forced perspective! [chuckles] The castle uses it too. Your eye goes up, the castle feels HUGE. Your feet, meanwhile, feel the twenty thousand steps.

clues.clue: Walt's word for a tall landmark, like a castle or a mountain, that pulls guests deeper into a park.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is a weenie! [laughs] Walt supposedly named it after the hot dogs he used to lead his poodle around. Yes, really.

clues.clue: Walt's term for constantly improving an attraction or show, even after it's finished.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is plussing! [excited] Walt said Disneyland will never be completed as long as there is imagination left in the world. Plus it up, people!
